related_questions.snippet: About 15% of patients with Degos disease have long-term survival, with disease often limited to the skin and with no manifestations of fatal bowel or CNS involvement. text_blocks.snippet: Dercum's disease, also known as adiposis dolorosa, is a rare disorder characterized by painful, localized deposits of fat (lipomas) in the subcutaneous tissue, often accompanied by fatigue and other symptoms. The exact cause is unknown, but it's thought to involve both neurological and endocrine system dysregulation. Pain management is the primary focus of treatment, with various approaches including pain relievers, corticosteroids, and other medications, according to DermNet.
snippet_highlighted_words: a rare disorder characterized by painful, localized deposits of fat (lipomas) in the subcutaneous tissue, often accompanied by fatigue and other symptoms

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Dercum's disease primarily involves painful, localized lipomas, typically in the abdomen and extremities, according to the National Institutes of Health (NIH). Other potential symptoms include fatigue, easy bruising, headaches, stiffness, and psychiatric disturbances like depression or anxiety.

list.title: Causes:
list.snippet: While the exact cause is unknown, it's believed to be a combination of neurological and endocrine system issues, according to the National Institutes of Health (NIH). It can be associated with metabolic derangements like diabetes and dyslipidemia. Some cases may be inherited, with a dominant genetic pattern where only one copy of the altered gene is needed for the disease to appear.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: There is no cure for Dercum's disease, but treatment focuses on pain management. This can involve pain relievers (including opioids and NSAIDs), corticosteroid injections, calcium channel modulators, methotrexate, infliximab, interferon alpha, and other medications. Surgical removal of lipomas or liposuction may be considered in some cases. Non-pharmacological therapies, such as acupuncture and electrotherapy, can also be used.

list.title: Distinguishing from other conditions:
list.snippet: Dercum's disease can be challenging to differentiate from other conditions, especially fibromyalgia, due to overlapping symptoms like chronic pain and fatigue, according to the National Institutes of Health (NIH). It's also important to distinguish painful lipomas in Dercum's disease from other breast lumps.
